items.summary: fmgrep is a (Claude-powered) open source reimplementation of a FAANG code search engine I was involved in a few years back. It's aimed at very large (e.g. AOSP) source trees. Back then we wanted to get our hands on the Github search engine ( https://github.com/danlark1/sparse_ngrams ) but it was not available, so we went a different way. Instead of n-grams,`fmgrep` builds an FM index of the tree with O(pattern) `count` and O(occurrences) `locate`, which is quite cool and leads to blazing fast performance as seen in the benchmarks.

items.title: Show HN: Map of the Small Web
items.summary: After following the digital garden / small-web movement for the last few years, I was curious about mapping the small web. I gathered about 28K websites so far from existing directories like Kagi’s small web list, blogroll.org, blogscroll and a handful of manually added sites. The map clusters items together that (ideally) write about similar things. There’s a pretty heavy software bias in the data for now, so I’ll look into broadening the map in future versions. For now enjoy clicking through, finding new sites and exploring the map!
